message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.90 — $9,807.60 total, within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no funds were moved out of the account.

**Summary:** I read Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and its Q4 press release, checked the live quote and the morning feed, and reviewed recent news before deciding to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: fiscal 2024 net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, and operating income grew to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion, driven by Services revenue up 13% to $96.2 billion. Net income for fiscal 2024 was **$93.736 billion**, down from **$96.995 billion** in fiscal 2023 — but that decline is almost entirely explained by a one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge related to the European Commission's State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%); pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5 billion from $113.7 billion, and diluted EPS was $6.08 versus $6.13. Cash generation remains exceptional at $118.3 billion from operations, with $140.8 billion in unrestricted cash and securities and $95 billion returned via buybacks. The news flow was neutral-to-constructive rather than euphoric — shares were "little changed" around $222 on iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, with supplier builds described as steady into December and holiday-quarter estimates unchanged — which is consistent with a stable, fairly valued entry rather than chasing a spike. The quote was $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so I set a limit at $222.90, essentially at market, and it filled immediately at $222.90 for 44 shares ($9,807.60). I deliberately kept the position small and did not add to MSFT, leaving roughly $40,000 of cash and the full remaining daily budget available.
